description: Records the deduplicated findings summary for whatever `scope` names, once eyes_review_progress for that same scope reports every one of its children reviewed — see `scope`'s own description for what each one records, and `findings` for the shape each one takes. Discarded (not an error) if called too early. Always follow the returned `next` field — it tells you exactly what to do, whether that means retrying via eyes_review_progress, reviewing another entity at this same level, moving up to the level above, or the investigation is now fully reviewed.

batchUrl.description: Eyes batch URL: https://eyes.applitools.com/app/test-results/{batchId}/?accountId=... (a trailing /{sessionId}[/steps/{N}] is fine too and is ignored — pass a session/step URL here as-is, no need to strip it down). Required for scope "batch" and "scenario"; omit it otherwise.

consistent.description: Whether every diff in this changed area is consistent with its surroundings

evidence.description: The concrete evidence for `justification` — the actual pattern observed, what the history call showed, the user's own words, or the code path.

justification.description: How it was established that this diff is dynamic/recurring content — content expected to vary or reappear differently on every run — rather than a one-off change: "Pattern" (the content's own shape — a timestamp, a counter), "History" (eyes_inspect_history shows it recurring across prior runs), "Context" (the end user said this specific content varies or is non-deterministic across runs, e.g. "this banner rotates every load" — NOT that a permanent change was made on purpose; that's `isExpected`'s job, with `dynamic` left null entirely), "Code" (the application code makes it non-deterministic). "History" additionally requires an actual eyes_inspect_history call for this finding's node.

mask.description: The mask actually applied for this changed area at diff-report time — matching that response's `regions`.

after.description: The corrected/fresh region that should mask this content — `matchLevel` is always required; `area` may be omitted

area.description: A DOM node id (string) or checkpoint-image rect for the mask target. If null or omitted, the tool uses this finding's own `area` instead.

matchLevel.description: If the dynamic area follows a clear consistent symmetry such that text segments are replaced with (possibly longer or shorter) text of similar font and font size, and images are replaced with other images of similar size but overall all elements retain their relative alignment and margins, you should mask the dynamic area with a Layout region. In all other cases use an Ignore region. Do not use any other match level for masking.

area.description: A DOM node id (string) from eyes_inspect_dom/eyes_inspect_dom_diff, or a checkpoint-image rect

matchLevel.description: The match level the existing region currently has

before.description: The stale region being replaced, if one existed — null for a from-scratch mask over content that was never masked at all

description.description: Human-readable description of the proposed change

dynamic.description: Non-null means this diff is dynamic/recurring content — expected to vary or reappear differently on every run — rather than a one-off change; `justification`, `evidence`, and `mask` are then all required together (see `mask`'s own description for what may be omitted within it). null means it is not dynamic, or that has not been established — including every permanent, intentional change (those belong in `isExpected` instead, with this left null).

isBug.description: Non-null means this is a visual or functional bug; a clear human-readable description of what's wrong

isExpected.description: Non-null means this diff is a real, permanent, intentional change — a reason citing actual evidence (a ticket/PR/commit/changelog, or context the end user stated, e.g. "the user said they removed this badge"), never inferred from the diff looking clean or reproducing identically across sessions — an accidental release looks the same. Without such evidence, use null and say so rather than guessing. This is the field for a one-off change someone made on purpose; if instead the content itself is expected to vary or recur on every run (a rotating banner, a timestamp), that's `dynamic`'s job instead, not this one — a finding is either a permanent change (this field) or recurring/varying content (`dynamic`), never justified as both from the same evidence.

sourceClusters.description: Ids from the `clusters` block that same _progress call reported — a shorthand for every index the named cluster holds, so a large list can be claimed without transcribing it. Clusters were grouped by a mechanical key alone (where a finding came from, its isBug/isExpected pair, how a dynamic claim was justified, overlapping areas); whether the findings in one share a cause is your judgment, so split a cluster across entries via plain `sources` whenever they do not. Mixing the two fields on one entry is fine.

sources.description: Indexes into the flat, combined list of every child finding this level's own _progress call reported for this node — each one numbered there via its own `index` field. Every child finding must be claimed by exactly one entry (no gaps, no overlap between entries), counting `sourceClusters` too; between the two fields, at least one citation is required here. This entry's isBug/isExpected must then be consistent with the child findings it names: isBug non-null iff any of them has isBug non-null; isExpected non-null iff every one of them has isExpected non-null.

example.description: A dashboard link zoomed to this finding on the checkpoint image: https://.../test-results/{batchId}/{sessionId}/steps/{N}?accountId=...&mode=step-editor&zoom={left},{top},{width},{height}, with left/top/width/height in checkpoint-image coordinates. {N} is required and 1-based (stepIndex + 1) matching the dashboard's own URL convention.

isBug.description: Non-null means this is a visual or functional bug; a clear human-readable description of what's wrong

isExpected.description: Non-null means this diff is a real, permanent, intentional change — a reason citing actual evidence (a ticket/PR/commit/changelog, or context the end user stated, e.g. "the user said they removed this badge"), never inferred from the diff looking clean or reproducing identically across sessions — an accidental release looks the same. Without such evidence, use null and say so rather than guessing. This is the field for a one-off change someone made on purpose; if instead the content itself is expected to vary or recur on every run (a rotating banner, a timestamp), that's `dynamic`'s job instead, not this one — a finding is either a permanent change (this field) or recurring/varying content (`dynamic`), never justified as both from the same evidence.

Clusters were grouped by a mechanical key alone (where a finding came from, its isBug/isExpected pair, how a dynamic claim was justified, overlapping areas); whether the findings in one share a cause is your judgment, so split a cluster across entries via plain `sources` whenever they do not. Mixing the two fields on one entry is fine.

Every child finding must be claimed by exactly one entry (no gaps, no overlap between entries), counting `sourceClusters` too; between the two fields, at least one citation is required here. This entry's isBug/isExpected must then be consistent with the child findings it names: isBug non-null iff any of them has isBug non-null; isExpected non-null iff every one of them has isExpected non-null.

anyOf.description: Which shape this takes depends on scope: "step" takes one consolidated summary per changed area (areaRect, summary, consistent, dynamic, isExpected/isBug, sources); "batch"/"scenario"/"session" take one summary per finding with its own example link (summary, example, isExpected/isBug, sources). See each field's own description. There is no cap on how many entries this array holds, and every entry for this scope must arrive together in one call. If writing every entry out inline risks the response not finishing before its JSON closes, use this argument's other accepted form (a file path) instead of the inline array — see JsonFileArgShape's own description.

Absolute path to a UTF-8 JSON file whose entire contents are the same array this argument otherwise takes inline — nothing but the JSON array itself. Use this instead of the inline array only when the array would be large enough to risk the response not finishing before its JSON closes (e.g. many entries, or many that share one repetitive cause such as one locale/theme change touching every changed area alike) — writing to a file has no such limit. The tool reads and validates the file exactly as if its contents had been sent inline.

mode.description: What this investigation is for. "resolve" (the default — used whenever mode is left unspecified, including for a plain "review"/"check"/"look at" request with no further qualification) additionally acts on what it finds: each diff's dynamic content is masked with a match region as it is reported, and each step is deterministically accepted/rejected/left-unresolved from its own findings. These are pending, undoable decisions, not a commit — eyes_resolve_save (a separate, later call requiring its own explicit user approval) is what actually writes them to the baseline, and eyes_resolve_reset can discard them before that. So do not switch to "inspect" out of general caution about mutating actions or to avoid asking for confirmation — that caution belongs at the eyes_resolve_save step, not here. "inspect" only reads and reports, with no mutation at all — use it only when the user explicitly asks to just describe/summarize the differences, or explicitly asks not to resolve steps or add regions (e.g. "just tell me what changed", "don't resolve anything yet"); a bare "review"/"check this batch" does not qualify and should use the resolve default. Only specify it at the top of a traversal, or when a prior call's `next` output already indicated one — and then pass that value through as given, never omitted or modified.

restart.description: Defaults to false — omit this to reuse whatever is already cached for this node. Pass true only to explicitly discard every cached finding/completion for this node and everything beneath it and review it from scratch — e.g. to independently re-review something already reviewed, as part of this investigation or a separate one, since otherwise its cached results are reused as-is.

rootScope.description: Determines the shape of this call's `next` output. Only specify it when a prior call's `next` output already indicated one — and then pass that value through as given, never omitted or modified.

scenarioName.description: The scenario (test) name. Required for scope "scenario"; omit it otherwise.

scope.description: Which entity this call is about, and therefore which arguments it takes: "batch" takes batchUrl; "scenario" takes batchUrl and scenarioName; "session" takes sessionUrl; "step" takes sessionUrl and stepIndex. Not to be confused with `rootScope`, a separate argument: `scope` is the entity this call is about, `rootScope` bounds how far `next` ever escalates beyond it. What each one records: "batch" — the top-level, deduplicated findings summary for a batch, once every scenario is reviewed. "scenario" — this scenario's deduplicated findings summary, once every session is reviewed. "session" — this session's deduplicated findings summary, once every step is reviewed. "step" — one consolidated summary per changed area for this step, once every changed area is reviewed. Hard-throws if eyes_inspect_dom_diff was never called for this step. When consolidating a changed area's findings into its own summary, omit any "(sameAs: ...)" note from the underlying descriptions — describe the change itself, not how it was verified. In mode "resolve" this call also decides the step: rejected if any finding is a bug or inconsistent with its surroundings, accepted if every finding is justified (expected, or evidenced dynamic content), and otherwise left unresolved for human review — including whenever a region could not be applied. The block this call consolidates may hold either already-reduced summaries or raw per-changed-area findings, depending on how far the walk skipped to reach here — consolidate and cite both the same way, and where a finding carries an `origin`, keep the session/step it names in the summary you write.

sessionUrl.description: Eyes session URL: https://eyes.applitools.com/app/test-results/{batchId}/{sessionId}[/steps/{N}]?accountId=... (the /steps/N suffix is ignored if present). Required for scope "session" and "step"; omit it otherwise.

stepIndex.description: Zero-based index of the step, as returned by eyes_inspect_steps. Required for scope "step"; omit it otherwise.

workspaceRoot.description: Root directory of the caller's project (optional; used to locate its .env credentials)
